core.title: Domain modules import no runtime machinery
core.given: A non-test module in the domain role, outside the stack's excluded (vendored/generated) trees
core.when: it imports a specifier or references a global (newly added or already present)
core.then: It MUST NOT import any of the stack's forbidden runtime, framework or transport specifiers nor reference any of the stack's runtime globals that count as machinery.
prefer: Keep domain code as data-in / data-out logic.
Move runtime, server, transport or framework machinery to an outer layer and pass the needed value inward.

During GREEN: adapt at the nearest existing integration or presentation boundary, passing the smallest value or domain-facing collaborator the behavior needs; add a new boundary only when no existing one can express the current behavior correctly.
avoid: Wrapping a framework or runtime API in a domain-named helper and keeping the coupling.
Importing runtime machinery into the domain just to satisfy the acceptance quickly.
unless: Test files (of every kind) and the stack's excluded (vendored/generated) trees are never scanned.
A file that is assigned to no layer role is outside this rule, not in violation of it.
core.why: The domain expresses rules, not machinery; what counts as machinery (server, transport, runtime primitives) depends on the stack, but the obligation does not. The domain must be runnable with no delivery machinery started (e.g. no server); a reference to a runtime machinery global in a domain module means it is not.
evidence: The stack's domain-purity check reports no forbidden runtime/framework import specifier and no runtime machinery global use in any domain module.
The domain remains executable without runtime machinery (runnable with no server or other delivery machinery started).
verification: The check flags, in every in-scope domain module, each import specifier in the stack's forbidden runtime/framework list and each use of a runtime machinery global.

runtime_machinery = the stack's forbidden runtime, framework and transport import specifiers plus its machinery globals; the obligation is identical across stacks and only the list of machinery changes with the stack.
server_free_domain = the practical test: the domain must be runnable with no server (delivery machinery) started.
Do not scan test files (all test files, whatever their test kind; which files count as test files is classified by the stack's checker) or the stack's excluded (vendored/generated) trees.

Imports of external packages (outside the project graph) are not layer-direction-checked; the forbidden runtime/framework specifiers are still matched by this rule's list even when they are external packages.
A file assigned to no layer role is out of scope, not a violation.

fires: A non-test domain module imports a runtime or platform specifier from the stack's forbidden list (newly added or already present).
A domain module imports an HTTP/server or UI framework that the stack lists as forbidden machinery.
A domain module references a runtime global that the stack counts as machinery.
doesNotFire: A test file in the domain role imports the test runner's module.
Files in the stack's excluded (vendored/generated) trees.
A file assigned to no layer role.
An integration or presentation module importing runtime, platform or framework machinery.

neutralityNotes: Core is fully neutral. The Bun machinery list (bun:*, node:*, htmx, express, fastify, koa, Bun.) is supplied via idiom.forbidden_runtime_imports and idiom.runtime_globals. The Vite-sibling cross-reference and the detector/finding ids remain bunOnly. The all-test-files exclusion is a general exclusion kept in core unless/verification; bun.json gives no filename pattern, so no suffix.* key is used and test classification is left to the stack's checker. 'vendored/build directories' is quoted as-is for roots.excluded.
